summary: Grundy County tower on Palmer Mountain that Tennessee Landforms lists as removed; a town history column says the lookout's family lived at the tower.

facts.status_note: Tennessee Landforms lists the tower as removed; no source describes what remains on the site today.

events.note: A town history column says Isham Hobbs was the lookout at the Palmer Fire Tower and that his family lived in a house there. The passage gives no year.
Tennessee Landforms marks the tower removed. No removal year is given.

evidence.supports: Table numbers are state forest tower numbers from a 1976 list
evidence.quote: Numbers in the table (e.g., 4-7) are state forest tower numbers (district-tower) from 1976 list of towers

evidence.supports: Many towers removed; most locations are now private property
evidence.quote: Many have been removed, and most locations are now private property

evidence.supports: Family raised in a house at the Palmer Fire Tower on Palmer Mountain; father was the Fire Tower Lookout
evidence.quote: was raised on top of Palmer Mountain in a house at the Palmer Fire Tower where his father, Isham Hobbs, was the Fire Tower Lookout

evidence.supports: Division towers formed its fire detection network between 1933 and 1975
evidence.quote: Collectively, the fire towers formed the physical manifestation of TDF's fire detection network between 1933 and 1975

evidence.supports: Division was responsible for building 208 fire lookout towers, about 1930 to 1970
evidence.quote: The TDF was responsible for the construction of 208 fire lookout towers during the period between ca. 1930 and ca. 1970

evidence.supports: Many division towers removed or awaiting demolition, from disuse or expired leases
evidence.quote: Many of the 208 fire lookout towers once part of TDF's fire detection network have been removed or are awaiting demolition as a result of disuse or the expiration of lease agreements with private property owners

sources.title: David Patton, Palmer Town Historian (town history column, PDF)
Tennessee Division of Forestry Fire Lookout Towers, 1933 to 1975 (National Register multiple property documentation form)

notes_for_editor: Tennessee Landforms gives the removed status, elevation, county and the 3-22 number; those are solid. The staffing event rests on one undated family recollection in a Palmer town history column, and the passage gives no year. The Division of Forestry link is inferred from the state forest numbering; no source read names the agency for Palmer, so the story says 'suggests'. No build year, design or height appears in any source read. The record's registers field lists NGS with FC1885; Tennessee Landforms describes six-character PIDs like that as NGS datasheet IDs, so it is not a register listing. The NRHP form counts 208 Division of Forestry towers while the Landforms table has 275 entries; the two counts are not directly comparable.
